ug.title: UNLV International Undergraduate Admissions (requirements, deadlines, fee, codes)

test_policy.notes: ACT/SAT scores are not required for international students; first-year applicants who have taken either test are recommended to submit official scores. SAT 1120 or ACT 22 can substitute for the 3.0 GPA requirement.

requirements.notes: International first-year admission requires a 3.0 cumulative GPA OR SAT 1120 (EBRW + Math) OR ACT 22. Apply with the UNLV application or the Common App (no preference); $95 nonrefundable international fee. Send the high school transcript (certified translation if not in English; PDF with grading key) and proof of English proficiency; after admission upload the Confidential Financial Certification form and a bank letter for the I-20.

deadlines.label: Fall first-year priority deadline
deadlines.notes: To get priority for institutional grants and scholarships an applicant must be admitted and complete the Institutional Aid Application / Alternative Need Form by this date; applications open Oct. 1. The page prints no year; taken as the current cycle.

deadlines.label: Fall first-year application deadline
deadlines.notes: Spring deadline is Dec. 1. I-20 processing starts 6 weeks before the semester for initial F-1 applicants. UNLV's College of Engineering IEP page lists earlier dates (May 1 for fall), which were not confirmed on the admissions page.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Other accepted proof: SAT EBRW 480+, ACT English 18+, ELS Level 109, MET 53, CEFR B2, or ENG 113/ENG 101 with a C or better. Exempt: a degree from a U.S. institution; being from or earning a degree in a listed English-speaking nation (e.g. Canada excluding Quebec, Ireland, Nigeria, the Philippines, Singapore, South Africa, the United Kingdom); or a degree earned outside the U.S. where English was the primary language of instruction. Scores must be under two years old. English Language Center Fast Track: applicants who meet everything but English (TOEFL iBT 59-71 or new 3.0-3.5, IELTS 5.0-5.5, Duolingo 85-90, PTE 43-58) enroll full-time in the non-credit Intensive English Program; finishing Level 4 with a C or better satisfies the requirement without a new test.

english.notes: New 1-6 scale, tests from January 2026; no band below 3.5.

cost.notes: UNLV cost page (2026-27, 15 credits, two semesters): the tuition figures already include required fees and a one-time $200 new-student fee; international (F-1) $31,710 includes a $145-per-semester international fee; mandatory health insurance for international students is estimated separately. room_board = on-campus housing $7,424 + food $6,024; other_usd = transportation $1,360 + miscellaneous $3,304. Estimated nonresident total cost living on campus $50,284.

aid.notes: Admitted international undergraduates may be considered for merit-based scholarships of $5,000-$7,000 per year (once a year, fall entry only; must be admitted before the priority deadline and complete UNLV's Alternative Need Form). No need-based aid for international students is described, so that is left unconfirmed.

toefl.note: The UNLV international pages do not print a TOEFL institution code; select University of Nevada, Las Vegas when ordering.

tier_notes.business: Editorial judgment: the Harrah College of Hospitality is a nationally recognized strength; placed in the 41-100 band, not a published ranking.
